title: Hearing Tricky Sam and Kenneth Roane in Harlem cellars, 1924
summary: On his first, two-week visit in 1924 Waters toured Harlem's hundred-odd clubs and heard Tricky Sam Nanton playing with Kenneth Roane on curved soprano.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: 1924 I come to New York, that's my first time in New York - not to stay, but my first time in New York. But in two weeks time - in Harlem it was over a hundred clubs, you know. And I heard, that's where I heard Tricky Sam, the same trombone player that wrecked it, in little places. I even remember, I think I remember the name, it went Green Hornet or Green Dragon or somethin' like that, in Harlem around 30 somethin' street and Lenox Avenue, in that neighborhood. Anyway I may be not exact about the date, but he was down in the cellar playin'. And we heard, I went by and walkin' around, you know, and I heard somebody sound like a woman or child or person, you know. So I didn't know what it was, so I looked, went down, peeped in. I saw the trombone player, Tricky, was down there with a guy named Kenneth Roane. And Kenneth Roane wasn't playin' trumpet then, he played trumpet in this band at Charlie Johnson's also at some period for quite a while, first trumpet. And he was playin' soprano saxophone, little curved one.
PS: Same guy who played with like among other bands, he played with a band from Springfield, Ohio, the Cecil Scott/Lloyd Scott -
Anyway. that's yeah, dark, real dark guy. See, so that's when I first came to New York, when we only stayed two weeks. But I went all around different places, you know, see everything -
